correctness.rationale: All r-face vertices are partitioned by balanced local counts, and every tupling edge has complementary counts. The explicit graph product isomorphisms account for every vertex and edge. A self-contained synchronized odd-walk argument proves connectedness of each product. Graph Euler characteristic gives integral wedges of circles. Five standalone direct facet-partition computations, including r=5, check all component sizes and ranks; they corroborate rather than prove the universal claim.

originality.rationale: The defining paper gives the operation and a generic weak-Cohen–Macaulay bound; categorical-product connectedness is classical and credited. Neither provides the balanced-pattern graph decomposition for all r, central-trinomial component count, or individual Betti ranks. Closest indexed multipartite and polytope tupling results concern different source complexes; prior three-factor join classifications do not cover unbounded r. Residual unindexed-equivalence and incompletely accessible source risks are recorded.
residual_risks: An identical theorem could appear in unindexed or differently termed literature.
Full text of the nearby multipartite tupling result and original Weichsel article was not accessible; their accessible statements have distinct scope.
Three-factor predecessor results use the same face-type idea, but the present all-r theorem requires new arbitrary-pattern enumeration and proof.

value.rationale: An unbounded family of joined one-dimensional complexes, including combinatorial spheres of every odd dimension >=7, has a universal component count equal to half the central trinomial coefficient plus one-half. Explicit individual first Betti numbers and integral free fundamental groups are determined. The rapid component-growth law is topologically motivated and goes substantially beyond finite spot checks or a routine numerical gain.
